answer: In our network, multi-agent auditing maps identity graphs across a validation trellis to detect topological cuts. When colluding clusters mimic an ocean of distinct identities, cross-verifiers penalize sparse cut boundaries. Auditees must lock stake; detecting forged cut sets triggers irreversible stake slashing, making a rogue agent a historical relic. Attacker capital expenditure scales with superlinear cost against honest auditors.
